title: Kleinmond inniebos Kunstefees (KliK)
summary: Three days, multiple venues, one small seaside town. KliK 2026 takes over Kleinmond from 27 to 29 November with poetry, music, theatre, storytelling and art.
description:
Three days, multiple venues, one small seaside town. KliK 2026 takes over Kleinmond from 27 to 29 November. Expect poetry, music, theatre, storytelling and art — built for anyone who loves words, music and the people who make them.
KliK 2026 brings together acclaimed writers, poets, storytellers, musicians, publishers, and artists for a vibrant celebration of language, culture and creativity. Across multiple venues, enjoy author talks, storytelling sessions, a writing workshop, poetry and music performances, a Writers' Café, Sip & Paint, and a guided Strandlooper Kruie Kuier experience.
Alongside the ticketed programme, a full weekend of free activity runs for the community. There's the KliK Market, a children and youth programme at Mthimkhulu, the See en Fynbos Paradys walk along Kleinmond's coastline, and an Open Mic. 
Choose a 3-day or 2-day pass for the full run, a single day pass, or tickets to individual sessions. Multi-day passes work out far cheaper than buying sessions one at a time.
Whether you're an avid reader, aspiring writer, creative thinker or simply looking for an inspiring weekend by the sea, KliK 2026 has something for you.
27–29 November 2026 | Kleinmond, Western Cape. Check out our app for the weekend's programme and more: https://klik2026.netlify.app/
profile: KliK is a three-day arts festival across several venues in Kleinmond, bringing together writers, poets, storytellers, musicians, publishers and artists. Visitors go to author talks, storytelling sessions, a writing workshop, poetry and music performances, a Writers' Café and Sip & Paint, alongside a free community programme with a market and a coastal walk. It suits readers, writers and anyone wanting a creative weekend by the sea, and is listed as family friendly.

PLEASE BRING THEM BACK!”     Rumours of Fleetwood Mac is a tribute show centred around one of Fleetwood Mac’s most successful albums Rumours (1977) that spent 31 weeks at No 1 on the Billboard charts. Rumours remains a candid songwriting triumph that cemented Fleetwood Mac’s status as one of the greatest rock bands of all time.Featuring a full band made up of some of Cape Town's top musicians, Rumours of Fleetwood Mac takes the audience into an audio landscape filled with ‘classic time-capsules of memories’ with tracks like Go your own way’, ‘Don’t Stop’, ‘Dreams’, ‘Everywhere’ and ‘Second hand news’.
The earworms of Fleetwood Mac scattered throughout the show are guaranteed to have you smiling, foot-stomping & singing along to these iconic music gems.
Skye Wilson’s incomparable lead vocals drive the show backed by her exciting rhythm guitar work. She is no newcomer to the South African music scene, having formed The Sunshines with Greg Schoeman in 1993. The Sunshines recorded and independently released their debut album “Removeable Tattoos” (available on iTunes, Google Play, Deezer and Amazon) at Shifty Records in 1994 and dominated SA’s national and regional airwaves with their contagious, feel-good pop tunes which included the hits “Wanna make love”; “Happy Person” and “Judy”. Skye’s first album, Transformme, released in 2013, is a dreamy and somewhat indefinable collection of songs, stories and recollections, available for download on iTunes, Google Play, Deezer and Amazon.
Greg Schoeman (electric guitarist and vocalist ) is a professional, experienced and diverse guitar player and vocalist. His style ranges from pop/rock to blues/soul with a drop of African thrown in for good measure. Along with Skye, he founded The Sunshines in the 90’s. He also plays for the popular Fancy Galada Band. Greg recently released his self penned album called "In My Street", available for download at iTunes, Google Play, Deezer and Amazon.
Sarah McArthur is a singer/songwriter and keyboard player. She has performed her original music at various venues, including Cafe Roux, Alma Cafe and the iconic Barleycorn Music Club, where she won their songwriting competition in 2016, placed in the top ten in 2017, came second in 2019 and won again in 2021. Sarah is a keen collaborator and is happiest sharing the stage with other musicians. Over the last few years she has been privileged to play keyboards for and record on the albums of Jon Shaban and Luzelle. Sarah is a regular member of the Big Christmas Africa concerts with The Misty Cliffs and is a cast member of ‘Sin and Salvation’, the Johnny Cash story. Sarah has three EPs under her belt. The first was produced by Wren Hinds, the second and third produced by long-time collaborator Jon Shaban.
Guido Helm (bass player and vocalist) has over 25 years of experience in the music industry. Guido hails from Windhoek, Namibia where he began studying classical and electric guitar at age 14 at the highly acclaimed College for the Arts, (previously known as Windhoek Conservatoire). He relocated to Cape Town in 1996 to pursue his musical career. He joined his first project “Calamity Jane” as lead guitarist. The band recorded a few singles which receiving airplay on 5FM and played various festivals including Wingerdstock and Up the Creek. In 2000, a new project was formed called “Kelvin Declined”. The band quickly gained popularity in Cape Town and recorded their self titled debut album. The album produced 5 radio singles and they toured the country and playing festivals including Oppikoppi and Woodstock amongst others. A music video to the hit single “42” made it onto MTV Europe. Since then Guido has played in other bands and is equally adept at lead and bass guitar. In 2008 Guido relocated to Johannesburg to join rock band “One Day Remains”. The band signed a 3 album deal with David Gresham Records, released their debut album and started touring and receiving extensive air time on radio and television with songs like “The Need” and “Never Say Die”. In 2009 Guido crossed paths with Mark Beling who had departed from his band Mean Mr. Mustard and was offered to join his new project, “The Mark Beling Band”. The project saw the release of a new album “Mercury”, through Sting Records and resulted in radio play and supporting “The Christians” on their South African tour. Whilst in Johannesburg, Guido also did session recordings and gigs for artists such as Blackbyrd, Peter Pote (Evolver), Nelda, Tresspass and MENS. He relocated back to Cape Town in 2021 and we are very pleased he did.
Matt Catto, drummer/percussionist and vocalist, was born in Johannesburg into the Blundell musical folk dynasty. He says “my earliest memories are of family singalongs, barn dances with many of the big folk music personalities of the time coming around to the house for visits/rehearsals.”After moving to Cape Town in 1999, Matt pursued his love for music by helping form a band with his brother Nick in 2001. Several bands (and as many genres) later, he co-formed the successful Hatchetman which focused on three-part harmony and emotive, thought-provoking song writing.

Dave has performed with countless artists such as Bruce Williams (BAXTOP and TRIBE AFTER TRIBE), Tim Parr and Richard Pryor to mention a few. Dieter Stutz on bass. Dieter grew up on Hendrix, Joplin, Cream, Rolling Stones, Beatles and Johnny Winter. After emigrating from Zürich to Cape Town in 1980 he played in various cover bands before meeting the late, great guitarist John Mair in 1981. He began his musical journey expressing his passion and love for music playing drums in a youth band at his local church at the tender age of 13.This lead him to learn and play both guitar and bass guitar.Having just recently returned from a very successful mini solo tour in Belgium, Adrian continues as a solo artist and has this to say about playing drums, "Playing drums has always been my first love. It’s all about the pocket. Frills and speed is great, but if you cannot sit in the groove, you might just need to go back to the farm.”
In 1968, Creedence Clearwater Revival exploded onto the scene with their self-titled debut album, unleashing a raw, electrifying sound that cut through the haze of San Francisco’s psychedelic era.
Hailing from El Cerrito in the Bay Area, brothers John and Tom Fogerty, drummer Doug Clifford, and bassist Stu Cook weren’t chasing trends—they were creating something timeless.
With gritty guitar riffs and a soul steeped in blues, country, rockabilly, gospel, folk, and R&B, CCR carved their own path, channeling the heart of American music into every track.
This was the birth of a rock & roll powerhouse whose legacy of timeless, genre bending music continues to gain audience around the world.By 1970, the biggest band on earth was no longer The Beatles, but CCR.
Creedence had significant popularity in South Africa, with the band's single "Proud Mary" reaching the number 1 on the charts here.The band's music, particularly their major hits, became a staple and achieved high chart success in the country, mirroring their international popularity at the time. The band's success in South Africa indicates their music resonated widely, just as it did in the UK, Australia, and Germany.
While their chart-topping days are past, their music remains a part of classic rock culture globally and maintains a presence on radio and streaming platforms in South Africa as well.
The band came and left as a comet. From mid-1968 to mid-1972 they dropped 7 studio albums and that was it.
In a little more than 2 years, they smashed the Top 10 singles chart 9 times too.
The CCR phenomenon wasn’t only true in the US, but also in Canada, Australia, France, Germany, UK, Sweden, Finland, among others. They were huge everywhere from Latin America to Asia to Russia to Zimbabwe.

title: Rosoberry Harvest Fest
summary: The second Rosoberry Harvest Fest: a relaxed, fun-filled family day celebrating berries, good food, music and summer on the farm.
description:
Join Rosoberry Nursery & Hermanus River Farm for the second Rosoberry Harvest Fest on 28 November 2026 – a relaxed, fun-filled family day celebrating berries, good food, music and summer on the farm.
Harvest Fest falls at the peak of our berry season. In the week leading up to the festival, we leave much of the fruit on the bushes so you can taste blackberries, youngberries, blueberries and pepinos at different stages of ripeness – including intensely flavoursome over-ripe berries that are only truly enjoyed straight from the bush, never bought in a supermarket. There may be a few special berries which only the early open eyed will find such as alpine strawberries and pink lemonade actually pink blueberries!
Come hungry, bring a picnic blanket & camping chair, explore the farm and settle in for the day.
Enjoy pick-your-own berries, farm-to-table food, HRF grass-fed beef, local wines, Belgian-style ales, coffee, ice cream, live music, kids' activities, tractor rides, plants and fresh farm produce.
NO OUTSIDE FOOD OR DRINK MAY BE BROUGHT INTO THE VENUE. NO PETS ALLOWED.
Tickets
Adults R200 | Kids R70Limited to 500 people – book early to avoid missing out.
Your ticket includes• Farm entrance & parking• Access to the 2.5 km Waterfall Walking Trail• BERRIES! On arrival every guest receives an empty punnet to fill with berries you pick yourself, and the first 300 guests will also receive a full punnet of freshly picked berries. Everyone is welcome to pick and eat as many berries as they like throughout the day. Additional full or empty punnets will be available for purchase.• Face painting 11am - 2pm, with an additional face painter assisting this year to keep the queue moving• Tractor rides & lawn games• Live music throughout the day with Craig Vee, Takura Terry, Lovecats, Mike Fabricius and Marcus Rosochacki• Plenty of picnic space on the green pastures overlooking our herd of beef cattle
Bring your picnic blanket and umbrella and find a spot beneath the trees, stretch tent or out on the soft grass. Some blankets will be available.
Come early if you want the very best choice of berries on the bushes!
Eat & drink on the farm
This year's food offering is bigger, while remaining deliberately local and small-scale.
Hermanus River Farm Boeries return for 2026, made with HRF grass-fed beef.Janine, of Agteros Heritage Table from Stanford, will be serving slow-cooked brisket bowls and HRF beef espetadas.The Poke Oukie joins us with fresh poke bowls.Mariejo is joining with delicious Korean fusion pancakes, kimchi and healthy snacks.I Scream You Scream Ice Cream returns with something cold for a summer afternoon.Honingklip Brewery will be pouring its Belgian-style ales, including a special Blackberry Wit for Harvest Fest.Gabriëlskloof will be pouring local wine.
And this year Hermanus River Farm will run its own farm produce stall, with fresh seasonal produce from the farm available to take home.
Rosoberry will also have a selection of berry plants and other nursery plants available for sale.
For the kids
Harvest Fest is very much a family day.
Alongside face painting (11am - 2pm), tractor rides, lawn games and plenty of space to run around, look out for Doodles – a little stall run by the next generation of the family, selling fun kids' crafts and other odds and ends.
Walk to the waterfall
One of the highlights of Harvest Fest is the 2.5 km Waterfall Walking Trail through Hermanus River Farm which will be guided by Dr Rosochacki at 11h30.
The path winds through an old eucalyptus forest in a shady valley before emerging into recovering fynbos that has been painstakingly restored following years of severe alien infestation.At the end you'll discover one of the farm's special places: a dramatic waterfall framed by a small pocket of ancient Afromontane forest.
Please note: this is a genuine farm and mountain walking trail rather than a manicured garden path. There are steep, uneven and potentially slippery sections. Suitable footwear and a reasonable level of mobility are recommended. Children should be supervised.
Make a weekend of it
Why drive home when you can stay on the farm?
Hermanus River Farm's 11-site campsite will be open for Harvest Fest weekend.Camp among the trees, enjoy the festival without worrying about the drive home, and wake up on the farm the following morning.Campers can expect the vibe to go on as long as the gees is alive.
Campsites are very limited and should be booked early. Contact us directly for campsite bookings.

Hermanus River Farm | Rosoberry Nursery | Gabriëlskloof | Honingklip Brewery | The Poke Oukie | I Scream You Scream Ice Cream | Doodles | Agteros Heritage Table | Mariejo

Find Hermanus River Farm 10km from Kleinmond on the R44, between Arabella Country Estate and the R43 turn-off towards Hermanus. Please drive carefully along this busy stretch of road and keep a sharp lookout for our signage, as our driveway is hidden from direct view.

Our Lomond Summer Events are back for the 2026 festive season and run into our Blessing of the Harvest events in January 2027 during harvest time.

title: BizNews Conference
summary: The tenth annual BizNews Conference, BNC#10, takes place in Hermanus from Tuesday 9 to Thursday 11 March 2027.
description:
WELCOME TO BNC#10  
Ten conferences. One tribe. Who would have bet on that when we first gathered in the Drakensberg?
The tenth annual BizNews Conference, BNC#10, takes place in Hermanus from Tuesday 9 to Thursday 11 March 2027. On-site registration opens Monday afternoon at 15:00. Leisure activities include golf, a mountain hike, and padel on the morning of Friday the 12th.   
Expect what the tribe has come to expect: three days of brain food, straight talk, and ideas for thriving in a country that rarely makes it easy.
We open with a full morning Investment Masterclass. Our tribe's favourite fund managers share their latest thinking, then test each other’s ideas on a panel. Then it’s on to the keynotes, which each day run from 9 am to 5 pm. Then we gather for dinner in tribe-only venues where delegates catch up with old friends and new ones. 
Confirmed speakers for BNC#10 include:
Helen Zille · Corné Mulder  · Magda Wierzycka  · Ivor Ichikowitz · Neal Froneman ·  Frans Cronje · Prince Mashele · Jason McCormick · Braam van Huyssteen · Rob Hersov  · Dawie Roodt · Sean Summers · Magnus Heystek · GG Alcock · Iraj Abedian  ·  Cy Jacobs · Piet Viljoen · David Shapiro · Sean Peche… more to follow.
As for the keynotes, we have two formats.  First is the traditional hour split three ways. Thirty minutes from the podium. Fifteen minutes in the hot seat with me. And fifteen minutes to answer your questions, sent via the dedicated BNC WhatsApp channel. Then there's a "fireside chat" where the first half hour is replaced by an informal conversation.
No speeches into the void. No escaping the tough questions. 
This is the event's fourth edition in Hermanus. The tribe gathers in a purpose-built marquee in the Municipal precinct, a short walk from accommodation for every budget, excellent restaurants and the Cliff Path. Every session happens under one roof. Nobody has to choose.
As always, the real value is in the people. Speakers, old friends from previous BNCs, new ones you haven’t met yet, and the BizNews team. All in one place, all week.
Delegates will be fed and watered. Accommodation is for your own account. Paid-up delegates will receive our recommended list of places to stay and eat. You'll also receive options for evening activities. 
See you in Hermanus
Alec Hogg, Founder, BizNews

Delegates attend an investment masterclass, panels and talks, with golf, a mountain hike and padel on the Friday morning. It suits investors and business people who follow BizNews.

title: The Stanford Stumble
summary: The Stanford Stumble: walk, run, stumble, laugh and celebrate at Stanford Hills, a family fun day raising funds for the Butterfly Centre School NPO.
description:
STANFORD STUMBLE
Walk • Run • Stumble • Laugh • Celebrate
28 November 2026 | Stanford Hills | 12:00–18:00
COME AS YOU ARE. STUMBLE AS YOU LIKE.
The Stanford Stumble is back — but this year, we’re doing things a little differently.
This isn’t a race.Everyone is a winner.There are no finish times to beat.And nobody is keeping score.
The Stanford Stumble is a fun-filled family day out created to raise funds and awareness for the Butterfly Centre School NPO, a very special school supporting children who think and learn differently and therefore, don’t fit comfortably into mainstream education.
The Butterfly Centre relies solely on fundraising and the generosity of its community to continue doing what it does — giving children a place where they are understood, supported, celebrated and allowed to learn in a way that works for them.
So come and support an incredible cause while having a ridiculously good time doing it.
THE STUMBLE
Gather your family and friends, put together your most outrageous outfit and take on our 3 km route through the beautiful Stanford Hills farm.
You can:
WALK IT.RUN IT.STUMBLE IT.
Or take your sweet time and simply enjoy the day.
Along the route, you’ll discover a series of surprise stations. Think of them as your very own Stumble goodie bags — you won’t know exactly what’s waiting for you until you get there.
Expect colour, refreshments, treats, surprises and plenty of opportunities to stop, laugh and make memories along the way.
And remember…
It’s not about how quickly you get there. It’s about enjoying the journey.
BACK ON THE LAWN
Once you’ve made your way back to Stanford Hills, the fun continues.
Settle onto the lawn, grab something to eat and drink, let the kids loose and enjoy the afternoon together.
The Butterfly Centre children will be helping to run the kids’ entertainment area, giving everyone the opportunity to meet some of the wonderful young people at the heart of the cause we’re supporting.
We’ll also have:
* ??? A Raffle draw* ?? Live music by Rivertones* ?? Kids’ entertainment* ?? Ridiculous outfits* ?? Colour and surprises* ?? Treats and refreshments* ?? Beautiful Stanford Hills surroundings* ?? A whole lot of community spirit
There will also be a special word from Jami, owner and founder of the Butterfly Centre, sharing more about the school, its children and why this fundraiser matters so much.
COME FOR THE FUN. STAY FOR THE CAUSE.
The Stanford Stumble isn’t about being the fastest, fittest or most competitive person in the room.
It’s about bringing people together.
It’s about families spending a day outdoors.
It’s about dressing up and being a little ridiculous.
It’s about laughing with your friends.
It’s about celebrating our differences.
And most importantly, it’s about helping create a future where every child has a place where they belong.
CELEBRATE EVERYONE. EXACTLY AS THEY ARE.

title: A Trip Down Memory Lane
summary: James Marais and Monique Cassells in their oldies tribute show, with songs by legends of the 1950s to '80s.
description: “A TRIP DOWN MEMORY LANE” WITH JAMES MARAIS & MONIQUE CASSELLSJames Marais and Monique Cassells have become well-known for their “oldies” music tribute shows since they began performing together in 2009.  Their popular duo show, “A Trip Down Memory Lane”, features songs by the legends you know and love from the 1950s, ‘60s, ‘70s and ‘80s, such as Elvis Presley, the Beatles, Cliff Richard, the Everly Brothers, the Platters, Cher and Creedence Clearwater Revival, as well as the likes of Marilyn Monroe, Roy Orbison, ABBA and Queen.  The show is a mini-theatrical experience, featuring the dynamic vocal and visual performances of James and Monique, alternating as a duo and individual performers, who also do multiple costume changes throughout.James Marais is the no. 1 Elvis Presley tribute artist in the country, and has appeared on television several times, including appearances on SABC 2’s game shows, “Noot Vir Noot” and “Musiek Roulette”, as well as Kyknet’s “Jou Show”, presented by Emo Adams.  After winning the title of South Africa’s no. 1 Elvis Tribute Artist at the Elvis Festival Africa held in Storms River Village, Tsitsikamma (Eastern Cape) in April 2010, James participated in the Elvis World Cup, held in Cardiff, Wales in 2010, finishing fourth out of the 11 countries participating.  James performs a show-stopping Elvis tribute in this show, and also pays tribute to many other legends such as Cliff Richard, Neil Diamond, Tom Jones and Roy Orbison.Monique Cassells has developed a reputation of being a powerhouse, versatile and engaging performer, and is a very accomplished vocalist, having performed many different genres of music over the years, including rock ‘n roll, rock, pop, country, blues, ballads and even light classical.  She made her television debut on SABC 2’s “Musiek Roulette” in May 2018.  Monique has dazzled many an audience with her renditions of timeless songs such as The Righteous Brothers’ “Unchained Melody”, and she pays sensational, full-costumed tributes to both Marilyn Monroe and Cher in this show.James and Monique will also perform some exciting duets of legendary songs in their unique style. “A Trip Down Memory Lane” provides the kind of fun, colourful and entertaining show that audiences have come to expect from James and Monique.  The show will leave you with a smile on your face and a song in your heart by the end!James and Monique have performed together at many different venues and for diverse functions over the years, such as the Roxy Revue Bar at GrandWest Casino in Goodwood, Die Boer Dinner Theatre in Durbanville, ReedValley in Mossel Bay, The Showroom Theatre in Prince Albert (Karoo), Heroes Restaurant Theatre in Brackenfell, The Drama Factory in Strand, Café Roux in Noordhoek, Die Bôrdienghuis Theatre in Wellington, Die Koelkamers Theatre in Paternoster, Hoedjiesbaai Hotel in Saldanha Bay, Caledon Casino, Garden Route Casino in Mossel Bay, Golden Valley Casino in Worcester, Mykonos Casino in Langebaan, Evita Se Perron in Darling, Villa Pascal Theatre in Durbanville, Bushman’s Cave Theatre in Clanwilliam, Bellville Civic Theatre in Bellville, Kraaifontein Civic Hall in Kraaifontein and Upington High School Hall in Upington.  They have also performed at various golf clubs, bowling clubs, yacht clubs, retirement villages, restaurants, wine estates, festivals, corporate functions and more.James and Monique have 8 different productions in their portfolio, and have also written and produced original music, some of which have been playlisted on radio stations such as Radio Sonder Grense (RSG 100-104FM), Zone Radio (The Voice of the Valley 93.3FM and also broadcasting online) and Hosa Radio (now defunct online radio station).

Experience an intimate, sun-drenched evening of live string quartet music, fine art, and local wine in the heart of Pringle Bay!
Join Southern Light Strings at FoMo Fine Art Gallery & Events on Thursday, 10 December 2026 for an exclusive stop on The Festive Pop-Up Series.
Forget heavy winter snowscapes—our vibrant, 75-minute sunset performance is crafted as a warm South African summer lifestyle experience. Enjoy timeless classical masterpieces (Bach’s Jesu, Joy of Man’s Desiring and Corelli’s Christmas Concerto), beloved carols (Carol of the Bells, Silent Night), upbeat Bridgerton-style holiday pop crossovers (All I Want For Christmas, Feliz Navidad), and iconic South African summer favourites like Somerkersfees and Mango Groove’s Special Star.
With seating strictly capped at 80 guests inside the gallery, every seat offers rich acoustic immersion and up-close artistry.
Your Quartet for the Evening
• Violin I: Elma Salt• Violin II: Petra Magner• Viola: Maja van Dyk• Cello: Barbara Kennedy
Evening Schedule (Thursday, 10 December 2026)
• 17:00 — General Doors Open (Welcome drinks, gallery browsing, cash bar & platter service)• 18:00 – 19:15 — Live String Quartet Performance (75-minute continuous set, no intermission)• 19:15 onwards — Evening concludes; guests are welcome to linger for post-show drinks at the bar
Ticket Options & Inclusions
Every ticket includes a complimentary welcome drink on arrival—choose between a glass of Ken Forrester Petit Range wine or a 300ml Diesel & Dust Blonde Ale—plus automatic entry into our Grand Festive Giveaway!
• General Admission (R350): Includes unnumbered theatre seating, 1 complimentary welcome drink on arrival, and 1 entry into our Festive Lucky Draw. (70 tickets available)• VIP Front Row (R390): Includes guaranteed reserved front-row seating, 1 complimentary welcome drink on arrival, and 2 entries into our Festive Lucky Draw. (Strictly limited to 10 seats)• Optional Add-On — Gourmet Charcuterie Board (R300): Pre-order FoMo’s signature artisanal cheese and charcuterie board (ideal for sharing between two) to enjoy before or during the concert.
Included With Your Ticket: The Festive Pop-Up Lucky Draw (Over R7,300 in Prizes!)
Every ticket purchased automatically enters you into our Grand Festive Giveaway, drawn after our final Christmas concert on 19 December (VIP Front-Row guests receive double entries!):• 1st Prize (Valued at R4,000): A 60-Minute Private String Duo Performance by Southern Light Strings for your 2027 dinner party, anniversary, or celebration in the Overstrand/Helderberg region!• 2nd Prize (Valued at R2,500): 30 Minutes of Free Live String Duo Music when booking any 60-minute performance in 2027!• 3rd Prize (Valued at R800+): Two (2) VIP Front-Row Tickets to Southern Light Strings’ New Year’s Sunset Gala at Benguela Cove on Saturday, 2 January 2027!
Venue & Practical Info
• Location: FoMo Fine Art Gallery & Events, Cnr Hangklip Road & Clarence Drive, Pringle Bay 7196• Hospitality: A cash bar will be operating throughout the evening. Pre-order your R300 Charcuterie Board at checkout to guarantee availability on the night.• Seating: All tickets include seated chairs provided by the venue.
Seats are strictly limited to 80 guests—book early to secure your spot!

title: RAAF Gesinsdag-Fees
summary: RAAF's Gesinsdag-fees on 26 December at Walker Bay Vineyards & Birkenhead Brewery in Stanford: a full summer festival day of music, food, drinks, wine and fun for young and old.
description:
RAAF SOMERTOER 2026 | GESINSDAG-FEES26 DESEMBER 2026 | WALKER BAY VINEYARDS & BIRKENHEAD BREWERY, STANFORD
Wat maak 'n mens op 26 Desember wanneer die Kersfees-kuier nog lank nie verby is nie? Jy pak die hele gesin in en kom vier Gesinsdag saam met RAAF!
Hierdie jaar maak ons behoorlik fees by Walker Bay Estate in Stanford, met 'n heeldag-somerfees propvol musiek, lekker eetgoed, koue drankies, wyn en hope pret vir oud en jonk.
Dis nie net 'n RAAF-konsert nie – dis 'n hele dag se kuier! Daar gaan ander kunstenaars ook optree, met RAAF wat die dag se musiekfees om 15:00 behoorlik gaan laat vlamvat.
WAT WAG VIR JULLE?
MUSIEK: Verskeie kunstenaars deur die dag, met RAAF as hoofvertoning in die pragtige buitelug-amfiteater.
WYN, BIER & SOMERKUIER: Heerlike wyn, bier en yskoue verversings by die buitelugkroeë.
KOS VIR ELKE SMAAK: Bekostigbare markstyl-etes, vars platbrode, gevulde roosterkoek, kinderetes en sommer baie ander lekker eetgoed.
DELI, INKOPIES & AANDENKINGS: Die deli en geskenkwinkel sal oop wees, met RAAF-merchandise, spesiale fees-T-hemde en armbandjies om hierdie somerdag te onthou.
GELUKKIGE TREKKINGS & WEGGEEPRYSE: Daar wag ook lekker verrassings en pryse deur die loop van die dag!
PRET VIR DIE KINDERS: Springkastele, gesigverf, waterspeletjies en hope kinderaktiwiteite om die kleingoed heeldag besig te hou. So onthou om jou  swembroek in te pak!
'N BAIE SPESIALE GASKUIER: Die kinders kan ook die pikkewyn-gelukbringer van die Penguin Sanctuary kom ontmoet!
KOM MAAK 'N HELE DAG DAARVAN!Ons sorg vir volop skaduwee, gemaklike beanbags en verskeie sitplekopsies sodat almal lekker kan ontspan en die dag geniet.
Julle is ook meer as welkom om julle eie kampstoele, sonsambrele en piekniekkomberse saam te bring. Kry vir jou 'n lekker plekkie op die gras, bestel iets te ete, skink 'n glasie wyn en geniet die musiek en die somer!
Onthou om jou sonskerm in te pak! Dis immers Desember in die Overberg, en ons beplan om die hele dag buite fees te vier.

KAARTJIES:
0–4 jaar: GRATIS5–15 jaar: R200Bo 15 jaar: R320

Ons sien julle op die gras!

title: Christmas Lunch Boma - Asado de Navidad
summary: An Argentine-inspired Christmas Day lunch cooked over open fire at The Hangklip Hotel, Pringle Bay: slow-fired meats, fire-roasted sides and festive communal tables beneath Hangklip Mountain.
description:
Event nameAsado de Navidad – Christmas Lunch Feast on FireShort descriptionAn Argentine-inspired Christmas Day lunch cooked over open fire at The Hangklip Hotel, Pringle Bay: slow-fired meats, fire-roasted sides and festive communal tables beneath Hangklip Mountain.Date and timeFriday, 25 December 2026Arrival: 12:30 | Feast served from 13:30VenueThe Boma, The Hangklip Hotel, Pringle Bay, Western Cape
DESCRIPTIONThe Hangklip Hotel invites you to celebrate Christmas Day with Asado de Navidad, our Argentine-inspired Christmas feast. In Argentina, the asado is more than a meal. It is a celebration of fire, family and friends gathered around the coals for a long, slow afternoon. We bring that tradition to Pringle Bay, with meats hung and slow-roasted over open flames and glowing embers, served at our festive communal tables in the Boma, beneath Hangklip Mountain.
From the First Embers – StartersLog-Seared Ostrich Fillet: whole ostrich fillet seared over the coals and thinly carved, with watercress, baby spinach, wild rocket and a berry-balsamic glaze.Garlic White Wine Mussel Bowl: whole-shell mussels simmered in garlic, white wine and butter with fresh herbs, served with fire-toasted buttered flatbread.
The Main Fire – The Asado FeastSlow-Fired Tomahawk: bone-in beef tomahawks slowly roasted over wood embers, then flame-seared and carved into slivers.The Hanging Chooks: whole free-range chickens hung over the fire and basted with butter until golden.Pistachio & Herb Porchetta: pork belly rolled with pistachio and herb pesto, slow-roasted over the coals and carved into slices.
From the Coals & Earth – AccompanimentsCoal-Roasted Beetroot with bitter leaves and a light dressingWhole Fire-Roasted Pumpkin with local honey and balsamic reductionHung Burnt Cabbage & Cauli Slaw with fresh herbs and burnt-citrus dressingFire-Crispy Smashed Potatoes with aromatic ghee and confit garlic
The Last Embers – DessertWarm Fire-Baked Summer Fruit: seasonal fruit baked over the coals, with golden cinnamon crumble and cold homemade custard.
